title: Throughput over single-thread: optimize for TLP not ILP
where_in_paper: Introduction and Table 1 Commercial server applications and Figure 1 TLP vs ILP
decision: Take radically different approach focusing on multithreaded throughput rather than single-thread frequency and ILP techniques like multiple issue, out-of-order, aggressive branch prediction; optimize for commercial server workloads
alternatives_or_rejected: Past two decades focus on single-thread desktop performance via higher frequencies, ILP exploitation (multiple issue, out-of-order, branch prediction) which shows diminishing returns due to memory latency and low ILP, leading to explosion in complexity and power; SMP of ILP processors is neither power nor cost efficient
rationale: Commercial server apps (Web99, JBB, TPC-C, SAP) have low ILP due to large working sets, poor locality, high cache miss rates, hard-to-predict branches, but high client-request level TLP; key metric is sustained throughput of requests not single thread latency; exploiting TLP hides memory latency and improves performance per watt, critical for data centers where power density 400-700 W/sq ft exceeds typical 70-150 W/sq ft
outcome: Designed for ~60W, appears as 32 discrete processors to Solaris without modification, simple pipeline requiring no special compiler scheduling, performance scales almost linearly with threads in lab on real commercial apps showing no bandwidth bottlenecks

title: 8 simple single-issue 6-stage cores each 4-way fine-grain multithreaded = 32 threads
where_in_paper: Niagara overview and Sparc pipeline and Pipeline interlocks and scheduling
decision: Implement eight Sparc pipes each as single-issue 6-stage pipeline (fetch, thread select, decode, execute, memory, writeback) sharing pipeline among 4 threads in a thread group via zero-cycle switch, round-robin LRU priority to least recently used, for total 32 hardware threads; threads become unavailable on long-latency events like load, branch, multiply/divide, trap
alternatives_or_rejected: Complex out-of-order superscalar or SMT sharing issue window each cycle; coarse-grain switch-on-event with context switch cost; chip multiprocessing of large ILP cores from previous generations
rationale: Simple core aggregated on single die with shared on-chip cache gives area and power efficiency, sharing pipeline among threads hides memory and pipeline stalls; fine-grain multithreading with zero penalty allows pipeline to do useful work every cycle; single-issue means no dependency checking between instructions from same thread needed (only one instruction in pipeline per thread), no branch prediction logic needed otherwise; simple pipeline results in higher throughput via overlapped execution
outcome: Eight instructions per clock peak across chip (one per pipe), fetch two instructions per cycle with predecode bit for long latency, full bypassing within thread for RAW, 3-cycle load latency with speculative issue of dependent instruction at lower priority; fair divider scheduling by LRU

title: Memory subsystem scaled for 32 threads: crossbar, banked 3MB L2, 4 DDR2 controllers
where_in_paper: Niagara overview crossbar and Memory subsystem
decision: Provide memory subsystem consisting of on-board crossbar >200 Gbytes/s with 2-entry queue per source-destination pair up to 96 transactions, 3-Mbyte shared L2 cache 4-way banked and pipelined 12-way set-associative to minimize conflict misses from many threads, interleaved at 64-byte granularity, plus four independent on-chip DDR2 channels >20 Gbytes/s up to 128 Gbytes capacity
alternatives_or_rejected: Private L2 per core or off-chip memory controllers and low-frequency off-chip buses/links that cause high latency coherence misses; conventional SMP with discrete processors
rationale: Having 32 threads places heavy demand on memory system for high bandwidth; commercial code has data sharing leading to high coherence miss rates that would go over low-frequency off-chip links; shared on-chip L2 eliminates those misses and replaces with low-latency shared-cache communication; banked pipelined design supports bandwidth, 12-way reduces conflict from many threads
outcome: Load miss delivered to source L2 bank with replacement way, directory shadows L1 tags, miss address entered, line fill returned to L1; crossbar is point of memory ordering, ensures fairness via age-based priority; I/O DMA ordered through L2; observed linear scaling indicating no bandwidth bottleneck

title: Tiny write-through L1s with simple coherence and compact windowed register file
where_in_paper: Memory subsystem L1 caches and Integer register file
decision: Use small L1s: 16KB 4-way set-assoc 32-byte block I-cache with random replacement and 8KB 4-way 16-byte line D-cache writethrough, allocate on load no-allocate on store, lines only valid/invalid, plus directory at L2 maintaining sharers list at L1-line granularity; implement windowed register file as 640 64-bit registers (5.7KB) with innovative split between fast RF cells for working set (visible window) and compact 6T SRAM cells for architectural set (all windows), linked via transfer port on window change
alternatives_or_rejected: Large L1s to reduce miss rate significantly, writeback L1 with MESI, and multiported large register file with many ports; paper says L1s must be much larger for significantly lower miss rates so tradeoff not favorable for area, and threads hide L1/L2 miss latency; traditional register file with many ports would be major area/access time challenge
rationale: Even though L1 small with ~10% miss rate per thread, four threads in group hide latencies; small caches significantly reduce average access time and good tradeoff between miss rates, area, and ability of other threads to hide latency; writethrough simplifies coherence protocol, stores attain global visibility in L2, store buffers (four 8-entry per thread) support bypass for RAW; register file sharing read circuitry because only one thread reads per cycle, window slide up/down on call/return triggers transfer taking 1-2 cycles while other threads continue
outcome: Simple coherence: load miss entered in directory, invalidates queued to sharers, copyback L2 writes back dirty evicts; L1 cache fetch uses two instructions per cycle with free slot for fill without stall; register file achieves single-cycle access with compact footprint

title: Low-power area-efficient design via simple pipeline sharing and low frequency
where_in_paper: Introduction power discussion and hardware multithreading primer
decision: Deliberately target low power ~60-72W at low clock (~1.2 GHz mentioned in related material but paper says ~60W) by using simple in-order pipeline, sharing pipelines among multiple threads, and not pushing envelope on CPU clock frequency, versus pushing ILP with high frequency
alternatives_or_rejected: Running ILP processors in server clusters at lower clock to reduce power (proportional loss in performance makes less desirable) or building aggressive out-of-order superscalar at high frequency as in P4/POWER4 era which incurs high power and complexity costs for little gain on commercial workloads (Figure 1 shows ILP processor mainly reduces compute time but memory dominates)
rationale: Data centers constrained by power supply and air conditioning, cannot hold complete complement of servers; requirement for commercial servers is performance per watt not single-thread; exploiting TLP improves performance without pushing frequency; sharing CPU pipelines among threads enables area and power efficient design; simple pipeline requires no branch prediction logic and no dependency checking
outcome: Niagara represents first in line of thread-rich processors providing high throughput and high performance per watt on commercial server applications, enabling high compute density; paradigm shift from ILP-focused designs; existing Solaris multithreaded apps run without modification
